turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Mr. Hale. Thank you for seeing me.

I have twenty minutes. Then I'm on a client call.

I got your voicemail after the zero was already in the system. That's the order I'm stuck on.

Owen says he wrote that essay himself. I'm here to find out what you actually have.

What is the evidence, specifically? Not the percentage. What did you see, and when?
Before we start, I reread Owen's last three essays this morning.

Good. That's a start.

Which three? Titles and dates, please.

And what did you find? Rereading isn't a finding.

One more thing first. Has anything been said to the class about this? Anything at all?
He writes like someone who was read to every night. That was you, wasn't it?

That's kind. It's also not evidence.

Yes, I read to him. His father did too. That tells you nothing about Tuesday's essay.

You didn't answer me, Mr. Hale.

Has the class been told anything? Yes or no.

And which three essays? Dates, please.
You've raised a genuinely thoughtful kid. I mean that.

Thank you. It doesn't change my question.

That's the third time I've asked. You've given me a compliment twice and no answers.

Has the class been told? Yes or no.

Which essays did you reread? Titles, dates.

I have eighteen minutes.
Which is why I'd hate for this to become a fight between two people who obviously both care about him.

I'm not fighting you. I'm asking questions.

You can end this in one sentence. Has the class been told?

Then show me what you have. The checker's report. The date you ran it. Which tool.

Claire's zero stood for months at this school. Four years ago. I remember the date.

I won't be walking out of here with "we both care."
